source.summary: GitHub Actions ‘Embedder footprint’ runs for PR #300 (branch fix/188-superinstruction-selection at head 3421c442138fb8dc2a8a41ee06db11e3f6f67bb9 — branch commit 3ca9974 (quarantine benchmark-shaped recognizers behind a runtime flag (#188)) on current main 93581e8 (PR #298, #134), and fix commit 3421c44 (move the vm-profile corpus workloads out of docs/ into tools/vm-profile/, a pure rename answering a Codex P1 finding); ubuntu-24.04, Rust 1.96.0): workflow_dispatch runs 45398465490 and 45398481840 against the branch and pull-request run 45398441987, which built the same tree, produced byte-identical sizes for every gated series
source.derivation: Re-baseline for PR #300 (#188, superinstruction selection: quarantine the benchmark-shaped recognizers behind a runtime flag). The PR adds RecognizerConfig (RuntimeConfig.recognizers, benchmark_shaped default false, CLI --benchmark-recognizers) and reconnects the previously dead recognizer pass (apply_benchmark_shaped_recognizers) in instantiate.rs behind that flag; the list_crc quickening is deliberately not referenced, because referencing its handlers resurrects about 60 KB of dead-code-eliminated .text for a quickening that can never fire. A Codex P1 fix on top moves the two executable vm-profile corpus workloads (json_agg.rs, text_index.rs) out of docs/benchmarks/vm-profile/ into tools/vm-profile/, as AGENTS.md prohibits executable measurement code under docs/; the move is a pure rename and does not change any gated size. Attribution was isolated by measuring current main alone (workflow_dispatch run 45398496895, gate success), which reproduces the checked-in baseline exactly on all 32 gated series, so every delta below is this PR's own. 28 of the 32 gated series change — every configuration that links the telomere library grows; the baseline configuration, which links no telomere code, is byte-identical in both profiles. In release, stripped file grows by 4,472 B in core-jit to 6,680 B in core-aot (stripped .text +3,408 B to +5,312 B): core +6,120 B / +4,768 B, component +6,072 B / +4,720 B, wasi +6,056 B / +4,720 B, core-nosimd +6,136 B / +4,768 B, wasi-threads +6,184 B / +4,864 B. In release-size, stripped file grows by 3,312 B in core-jit to 4,928 B in core-nosimd (stripped .text +2,400 B to +3,632 B). Against the original #164 baseline, the largest cumulative growth is now the release core-nosimd stripped file series at +9.91% (1,275,448 B to 1,401,864 B), overtaking the release component stripped file series at +9.85% (2,433,656 B to 2,673,416 B). The core-aot configuration, added by PR #267 after the #164 baseline, is not part of the cumulative comparison. Run-to-run spread was again 0 B for every gated series across the three samples.
